clue.text: She may be here, on the shelf

definitions.text: She may be here, on the shelf

blocks.clueFragment: She may be here, on the shelf
blocks.note: surface reading: a spinster, a woman left on the shelf, waiting somewhere
setter's reading: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard, a book kept on a shelf in a building full of books

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the shelf' is the old phrase for an unmarried woman; here the shelf is literal and She is a book title.
explanation.definitionFit: A building or room where books stand on shelves for borrowing, so a novel called She would be found there.

clue.text: Toy duck sat on by member

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece sitting on top comes first, the one sat on follows below

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, written as O

explanation.surface: A toy duck with someone's leg resting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish interlocking plastic bricks are a well-known children's construction plaything.

clue.text: Laud 'Dr No', the Bond novel for violence?

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective for sensational melodrama; the query flags the loose fit

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters come out in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praising Dr No as the Bond book for action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like part of the Bond story, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes sensational stories full of fighting and melodrama, the kind of violent action the clue names.

clue.text: Well-read, two accounts about Ms Moore?

indicators.note: about means around, so one account wraps round the name

blocks.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, twice
Demi Moore is the American film actress

explanation.surface: Is the actress Demi Moore bookish?
explanation.walkthrough: The second AC opens up to hold DEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly and learned people are widely read, so this adjective for intellectual pursuits fits.

clue.text: Sing in Tokyo, delightfully

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the following words

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the city and start of the adverb

explanation.surface: Performing beautifully in Japan's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto, an Alpine style.

clue.text: At which there may be a queue to kiss chief

definitions.text: At which there may be a queue

blocks.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
top as in the top person, the chief

explanation.surface: People lining up to kiss the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers wait in line at the roadside place where public transport vehicles halt to pick people up.

clue.text: Social gathering in pub can end in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
taken as written

explanation.surface: A get-together in a pub that ends in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A country dance party, traditionally held in a farm building, is a kind of social event.

clue.text: Ridicule South African bore

blocks.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa(n)
to tire is to bore or weary

explanation.surface: Mocking a tedious South African.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses mockery and irony to expose foolishness, so it is a form of ridicule.

clue.text: Paused, to gain courage before diving in?

definitions.text: to gain courage before diving in?

blocks.note: first meaning: stopped briefly to compose oneself

blocks.clueFragment: to gain courage before diving in?
blocks.note: second meaning, playful: filled the lungs before plunging into water

explanation.surface: Someone steadying their nerve on the diving board.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhaling deeply is what people do when they pause to steady their nerves, and swimmers do it literally before going under.

clue.text: Incompatible Europeans, getting on a bit

blocks.note: people from Poland
taken as written
a part is a bit

explanation.surface: Mismatched Europeans getting on slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on a bit' reads as growing old; 'getting on' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Things at opposite ends of the earth are totally different, which is the idiom for having nothing in common.

clue.text: Male bird biting head of one very large duck

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of one is kept
something biting takes the other pieces between its jaws, so they sit inside it

blocks.note: a gander is a male goose
first letter of one
OS is short for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: A gander pecking at an enormous duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very large duck' reads as one phrase, but duck alone is the definition; OS (outsize) is a clothing-size abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a species of fish-eating sawbill water bird belonging to the duck family.

clue.text: Bait ugly cave-dweller

blocks.note: first meaning: to provoke or goad, as an internet nuisance does
second meaning: a monster from Scandinavian folklore living in caves or under bridges

explanation.surface: Taunting a hideous creature in its lair.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to provoke people deliberately; as a noun it is the folklore giant or dwarf of hills and caves.

clue.text: I refused male lead in dreadfully cast operetta

indicators.note: something dreadfully cast is thrown about badly, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for male
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor turning down the leading role in a badly cast light opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Male lead' reads as one role, but male is just M and lead joins the fodder; 'cast' belongs to the anagram signal, not to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Die Fledermaus (The Bat) is Johann Strauss II's famous Viennese comic light opera of 1874.

clue.text: Crude, for the most part, my pal and I spoiled party in Wales

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped
spoiled things are ruined and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
taken as written, and dropped

explanation.surface: A crude remark from a friend ruins a Welsh party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a social gathering, but it is the political sense: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid Cymru is the nationalist political party of Wales, campaigning for Welsh independence.

clue.text: Dream is to settle in part of New York City

blocks.note: to long is to yearn or dream of something
taken as written
to land is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: Someone dreaming of moving to New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The island's western end holds the boroughs of Brooklyn and Queens, which belong to the city proper.

clue.text: Gift presented after the Italian's turned up for duty

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read from the bottom upwards
this piece is placed after the other in the answer

blocks.note: il is Italian for the
a gift is a talent or ability

explanation.surface: An Italian arrives with a present to meet some obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: A liability is something one is bound to pay or answer for, an obligation like a duty or tax.

clue.text: Look both ways

blocks.note: surface reading: road-safety advice to check left and right before crossing
setter's reading: a short word for a glance that reads the same forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: Road-safety advice before crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a four-letter palindrome: a word for a look that is spelt identically in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick or furtive glance, and its letters run the same in either direction.

clue.text: Major left on fabulous ship for small US island

blocks.note: major as in most important, key
L is the abbreviation for left
the Argo is the mythical ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: An army major left aboard a legendary vessel heading for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Key Largo is the largest and northernmost of the Florida Keys, a chain of small American islands.

clue.text: Audio tape contains a very small amount

indicators.note: the phrase contains the answer, which sits inside its letters across the word gap

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A cassette with barely anything recorded on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest Greek letter has come to mean a tiny quantity, as in 'not one jot'.

clue.text: Willing retainer? Mellors, say

blocks.note: game means willing, as in game for anything
a keeper retains or holds something

explanation.surface: A faithful servant: Lady Chatterley's lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Mellors is the estate worker who is Lady Chatterley's lover in D. H. Lawrence's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellors is employed to protect the game birds on the Chatterley estate, an example of that job.

clue.text: Verse - reportedly little boy's second in mag

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the name is taken by its sound
the second letter in the word is the one kept

blocks.note: Stan is a short boy's name, and its possessive is said with a Z sound
second letter of mag

explanation.surface: A boy's poem printed in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Invite round promising a list of engagements

blocks.note: to court is to invite or woo
circular means round

explanation.surface: Asking someone over with the promise of a full social diary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Court Circular is the daily published record of the British royal family's official engagements; 'promising' plays on engagements as promises to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official daily bulletin recording royal appointments and duties attended by the monarch and family.

clue.text: Film director, top artist

blocks.note: a cap is a top or lid
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

explanation.surface: A leading artist who makes films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top artist' reads as a compliment, but top is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Capra made It's a Wonderful Life and other Hollywood classics as a movie director.

clue.text: Famous launch? No end

definitions.note: used as an adjective, as in a star player

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a start is a launch

explanation.surface: A celebrated launch that never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means outstanding and celebrated, like a star attraction or star witness.

clue.text: Opening for Middlesex, I make a careless mistake over fieldsman

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter
turned over means flipped, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: first letter of Middlesex
taken as written
to nod is to slip up, as in 'even Homer nods'

explanation.surface: A Middlesex opening batsman blunders and is caught by a fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: Middlesex is an English county cricket team; mid-on is a fielding position near the bowler on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the term names a fielding position, and by extension the player stationed there.

clue.text: I'm left with social worker that's influential

blocks.note: taken as written
port is the left side of a ship
the ant is a social insect and a classic worker

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned with a social worker who carries weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a care professional; in crosswords it is often an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with great significance or power carries influence over events and people.

clue.text: Not prepared, a Parisian needing to get cash?

blocks.note: un is French for a
the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: A Frenchman caught short, needing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ready' (or readies) is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking readiness means not set up or equipped to act, as with Ethelred the Unready.

clue.text: Not the same second

blocks.note: first meaning: a different one
second meaning: one more of the same kind, as in a second helping

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a different one, and also an additional one, so both phrases fit as determiners.
